subject: series
synopsis: Alternate-dimension superhero team adventure.
author: Tony Bedard, Judd Winick

subject: series
synopsis: DC's out-of-continuity anthology of early-career Batman arcs by rotating creative teams (1989-2007) — Shaman, Gothic, Venom, Prey and more.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1970 adaptation of Robert E. Howard's Cimmerian: Roy Thomas and Barry Windsor-Smith's acclaimed opening, then Thomas and John Buscema's long tenure.
author: Jim Owsley, Michael Fleisher

subject: series
synopsis: John Byrne's 1987 post-Crisis relaunch of Superman, then Dan Jurgens's long tenure through The Death and Return of Superman and Jeph Loeb's run.
author: Dan Jurgens, Jeph Loeb

subject: series
synopsis: Lucasfilm's official Star Wars fan magazine: interviews, behind-the-scenes features and occasional short comics and fiction.

subject: series
synopsis: Tim Drake's first ongoing (1993-2009): Chuck Dixon's long street-level run, then Bill Willingham's War Games era with Stephanie Brown, and Adam Beechen.
author: Chuck Dixon, Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: MLJ's Golden Age anthology that introduced The Shield and, in #22 (1941), Archie Andrews, gradually becoming an Archie humor title.

subject: series
synopsis: The original X-Men (1963-1970): Lee and Kirby's founding team, Roy Thomas, and Neal Adams's acclaimed final run, before reprints from #67.
author: Arnold Drake, Dennis O'Neil

subject: series
synopsis: Spider-Man's team-up title (1972-1985): done-in-one pairings across the Marvel Universe, highlighted by Chris Claremont and John Byrne's stretch.
author: J.M. DeMatteis, Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Cable's first ongoing (1993-2002): Nathan Summers' time-tossed soldier stories, best in Joe Casey and José Ladrönn's run, before becoming Soldier X.
author: Joe Casey, Joe Pruett

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld and Fabian Nicieza's 1991 relaunch of the New Mutants as Cable's paramilitary team, later John Francis Moore's road-trip era.
author: Fabian Nicieza, John Francis Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Collects Batman issues from DC Rebirth era, featuring Tom King's run with stellar artwork showcasing Gotham's detective noir elements.
author: Tom King

subject: series
synopsis: Bart Allen, the hyperactive teenage speedster. Mark Waid's run is endearing and charming — young superhero done right, with genuine wit and a light touch on character development.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Dick Grayson's Rebirth-era series (2016-): Seeley, Percy and Jurgens, then Tom Taylor and Bruno Redondo's acclaimed Blüdhaven run.
author: Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: 2000 AD's companion magazine focused on Judge Dredd and the wider Mega-City One universe. Some of the finest Dredd stories appeared here — the format allows for longer, more ambitious narratives than the weekly anthology.
author: John Wagner

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis's Crossed universe expanded into an anthology of extreme horror scenarios. Aggressively transgressive — infected humans act on their worst impulses. Some intelligent story threads; largely relies on shock. Not for the faint-hearted.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's second What If...? series (1989-1998): alternate outcomes of Marvel stories, one premise per issue, from rotating creative teams.
author: Jean-Marc Lofficier, Randy Lofficier

subject: series
synopsis: Erik Larsen's creator-owned Image series (1993-), written and drawn by Larsen in real time as the finned cop Dragon ages and passes the book to his son.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's flagship anthology (1986-2000) that launched Paul Chadwick's Concrete and Frank Miller's Sin City alongside dozens of indie features.

subject: series
synopsis: Reprint collections of Chris Claremont and Alan Davis' original Excalibur series, the beloved British-based X-Men spinoff that mixed superhero action with interdimensional adventure and a distinctly wry humor, featuring some of Alan Davis' most acclaimed artwork.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Hanna-Barbera's mystery-solving gang in comics form. Gently educational mystery formula executed with warmth and humor.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2022 Amazing Spider-Man relaunch, mostly Zeb Wells with John Romita Jr. and Ed McGuinness, then Joe Kelly — a divisive run.

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell and Chris Bachalo's 1994 school series for teen mutants under Banshee and Emma Frost at the Massachusetts Academy.
author: Brian Wood, Scott Lobdell

subject: series
synopsis: DC's companion anthology to House of Mystery, running from 1956–1978 and hosted by Abel. Notable for featuring the original Swamp Thing story by Len Wein and Bernie Wrightson in issue #92.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Spider-Man's third monthly (1985-1995): done-in-one and crossover stories by Fingeroth, Conway and Kavanagh, through Maximum Carnage.
author: Terry Kavanagh, Louise Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: Britain's long-running weekly children's comic: Dennis the Menace, the Bash Street Kids, Minnie the Minx and friends.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology that launched Ant-Man and Hulk before splitting into dedicated titles. A key document of Marvel's early mythmaking — the Thor-less era of Kirby monster stories is particularly charming.

subject: series
synopsis: Silver Surfer's 1987 ongoing: Englehart's return to space, then Jim Starlin and Ron Lim's Thanos stories leading into The Infinity Gauntlet, and Ron Marz.
author: Steve Englehart, Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' long-running female superhero team. Passion project indie comics with limited production values; historically notable as one of the longest-running independent female-led superhero titles.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's 2005-2013 X-Factor Investigations: Madrox's mutant detective agency in Mutant Town, a long noir-tinged character run continuing to #262.
author: Peter David

subject: series
synopsis: Full-color reissue of Robert Kirkman and Charlie Adlard's The Walking Dead, with new back matter.

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1992 X-O Manowar: Aric of Dacia, a Visigoth abducted by aliens, returns to the modern world in their stolen armor, through the Acclaim era.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantastic Four volume 3 (1998-2011): Lobdell and Claremont's return, Mark Waid and Mike Wieringo's celebrated run, then Straczynski and McDuffie.

subject: series
synopsis: The Marvel anthology that launched Iron Man and Captain America before splitting. Early Kirby Iron Man stories have wonderful mid-century sci-fi charm.
author: Larry Lieber

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's vertical-scroll digital anthology of X-Men vignettes. Jason Loo's Maggott revival and other character spotlights range from charming to disposable, but the format allows creative freedom.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's 1983 teen mutant series, highlighted by Bill Sienkiewicz's Demon Bear saga, then Louise Simonson, ending in Liefeld's Cable era.
author: Louise Jones Simonson, Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: A newspaper strip collection from the Oregonian showcasing comic serialization.

subject: series
synopsis: The fourth weekly Superman title (1991-2003), led by Louise Simonson and Jon Bogdanove through the Death and Return of Superman era.
author: Louise Jones Simonson, Mark Schultz

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 51-issue weekly follow-up to 52 (2007-08), counting down to Final Crisis across the Multiverse.
author: Paul Dini, Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Silver Age anthology series focusing on Superman's love interest Lois Lane, a mix of romantic comedy, adventure, and sci-fi typical of the era; notable for its often bizarre Silver Age plots.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Selina Kyle's 2018 series: Joëlle Jones's Villa Hermosa run, then Ram V's Alleytown arc and Tini Howard.

subject: series
synopsis: The Avengers' California branch (1985-1994, later Avengers West Coast): Englehart and Milgrom's run, then John Byrne's Vision Quest.
author: Roy Thomas, Steve Englehart

subject: series
synopsis: Continuation of the classic Scooby-Doo comics formula. All-ages mystery humor with reliable character dynamics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Quality Comics anthology where Plastic Man debuted (alongside Phantom Lady and others). Historically essential — Jack Cole's original Plastic Man stories are comics gold.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Yoshitoki Oima's deeply emotional manga about an immortal being learning humanity through repeated relationships and loss. Structurally unique — each arc ends in tragedy, accumulating into something profound about connection and mortality.
author: Yoshitoki Oima

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's reprint archives collecting Marvel's classic black-and-white Savage Sword of Conan magazine (1974–1995) — one of the greatest sword-and-sorcery comics runs ever produced, featuring Roy Thomas, Barry Windsor-Smith, John Buscema, Neal Adams, and other top talents working in an uncensored format that the monthly color comic couldn't match. Essential Conan reading.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: The Legion volume 4 (1989-2000): Keith Giffen and the Bierbaums' dark 'Five Years Later' reboot, then the post-Zero Hour relaunch of the team.
author: Tom Peyer, Mary Bierbaum

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology that co-hosted Nick Fury: Agent of SHIELD and Doctor Strange. The Lee/Ditko Doctor Strange stories in particular are hallucinatory early masterpieces.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Kubert and Robert Kanigher's Easy Company is among the finest war comics ever produced — gritty, humanistic, and consistently anti-war in spirit despite its genre. Kubert's art is unmatched in the genre.
author: Joe Kubert

subject: series
synopsis: DC's anthology blending war stories with horror, science fiction, and the supernatural; a fun genre mash-up with memorable concept stories.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Deadpool's first ongoing (1997-2002): Joe Kelly and Ed McGuinness's opening run that defined the Merc with a Mouth, then Christopher Priest.

subject: series
synopsis: Action Comics from its 2016 return to legacy numbering: Jurgens, Bendis's #1000 era, Phillip Kennedy Johnson's Warworld Saga and Mark Waid.
author: Mark Waid, Mariko Tamaki

subject: series
synopsis: DC's long-running (1941-1986) Superman-Batman team-up title, the definitive Silver Age partnership comic that established the World's Finest as an institution of DC storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore's landmark run on Swamp Thing (1983-1987) that transformed a minor horror character into one of the medium's greatest literary achievements — reimagining Swamp Thing not as a man transformed into a plant monster, but as a plant elemental who only believes he was once a man. Launched Moore's American career and influenced a generation of writers.
author: Len Wein

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to the Adam West television series, written by Jeff Parker. Remarkably faithful to the camp tone while delivering genuine craft. One of DC's most purely enjoyable digital-first series.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's (then Atlas) fashion/humor comics for girls. A product of its era — cheerful, wholesome, and revealing of mid-century gender expectations.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Dell's classic Looney Tunes anthology comics collecting adventures of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, and the full cast of the Looney Tunes universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns' 2005 Green Lantern after Rebirth: Hal Jordan restored, the Sinestro Corps War, the emotional spectrum and Blackest Night.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: Eiichiro Oda's relentless manga epic is the best-selling comic in history for good reason. Rich world-building, deeply lovable characters, and an ambition of storytelling scope that few long-form narratives match.
author: Eiichiro Oda

subject: series
synopsis: Dick Grayson's first ongoing (1996-2009): Chuck Dixon and Scott McDaniel's Blüdhaven run, then Devin Grayson and Peter Tomasi.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: ACG's horror anthology, the first ongoing horror comic. Pre-Code era horror that paved the way for EC Comics. Dark Horse's archive editions collect the essential pre-Code stories.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Oracle's covert team (1999-2009): Chuck Dixon's Black Canary-and-Oracle partnership, then Gail Simone's celebrated run adding Huntress.
author: Charles 'Chuck' Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Marguerite Bennett's DC series reimagines World War II in a world defended by its women: Wonder Woman, Batwoman, Supergirl, and others band together against Axis supernatural threats. A pin-up-inspired alternate history with an inclusive, ensemble heart.
author: Marguerite Bennett

subject: series
synopsis: Superman's team-up title (1978-1986), pairing him with a different DC hero each issue, including Alan Moore's Swamp Thing team-up.
author: Bob Rozakis, Paul Kupperberg

subject: series
synopsis: Oliver Queen's 2001 resurrection by Kevin Smith and Phil Hester, continued by Brad Meltzer and Judd Winick; files also hold Mike Grell's 1988 run.
author: Ben Raab, Kevin Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Gibbons and Tomasi's 2006 Green Lantern Corps, Guy Gardner and Kyle Rayner's companion to Johns' Green Lantern through Blackest Night.
author: Dave Gibbons, Keith Champagne

subject: series
synopsis: Nate Grey, the Age of Apocalypse refugee with omega-level telepathy. A premise that never quite found its footing; Warren Ellis's brief run is the best material.
author: John Francis Moore

subject: series
synopsis: The adjectiveless X-Men from #157 (2004-2008): Chuck Austen and Peter Milligan, then Mike Carey, before becoming X-Men: Legacy.
author: Chuck Austen

subject: series
synopsis: George Baker's gentle military comedy about a hapless Army private. Harvey Comics ran this for decades; the humor is dated but the character endearing.
author: George Baker

subject: series
synopsis: Saitama is a superhero who can defeat any enemy with a single punch, but struggles with the existential boredom of being too powerful. Written by ONE and illustrated by Yusuke Murata, the manga is a razor-sharp parody of shonen action tropes that escalates into genuinely spectacular battles while maintaining its satirical wit.
author: ONE

subject: series
synopsis: The Punisher's 1987 ongoing: Mike Baron and Klaus Janson's street-level run, later Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning.

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Mike McKone's 2003 Teen Titans: Robin, Superboy, Wonder Girl and Impulse mentored by the original Titans, later McKeever and Krul.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Batman in Detective Comics across various collected volumes, encompassing James Tynion IV's acclaimed run featuring Batwoman and a rotating cast of Gotham heroes fighting religious cults and the Joker War's aftermath. Tynion's run is particularly notable for building Gotham's supporting cast into a full ensemble.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: The official digitally colored edition of Eiichiro Oda's One Piece: Luffy and the Straw Hat pirates' quest for the legendary treasure.

subject: series
synopsis: The original DC anthology where the Flash (Jay Garrick) and Hawkman debuted. Essential golden-age DC history.
author: Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: Sholly Fisch and Dario Brizuela's delightful all-ages crossover series pairs Scooby and the gang with DC superheroes, Hanna-Barbera characters, and pop culture icons in breezy, clever one-issue mysteries.
author: Sholly Fisch

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Carey's long run took Charles Xavier and then Legion through ambitious character arcs. Si Spurrier's subsequent Legion-focused run is wildly inventive psychological superhero fiction.
author: Mike Carey

subject: series
synopsis: Digital anthology celebrating diverse Marvel characters and creators. Variable quality but often surprising — a showcase for underrepresented perspectives on the Marvel universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Benjamin Percy's extensive Krakoa-era Wolverine run exploring Logan's place in the mutant nation while dealing with his addictions, his past, and ongoing threats to Krakoa, bringing a literary noir sensibility to the character.
author: Benjamin Percy

subject: series
synopsis: Gosho Aoyama's Detective Conan / Case Closed is the longest-running mystery manga, following teen detective Shinichi Kudo shrunken to a child's body. Remarkably consistent quality across hundreds of cases.
author: Gosho Aoyama

subject: series
synopsis: Sheldon Mayer's charming DC series about two babies who speak their own language. Genuinely witty and inventive — Mayer's insight into childhood perception is endearing.
author: Sheldon Mayer

subject: series
synopsis: Harley Quinn tries to be a genuine hero in Gotham while chaos follows her everywhere.
author: Stephanie Phillips

subject: series
synopsis: Kon-El's first ongoing (1994-2002), Karl Kesel and Tom Grummett's Hawaii-set run; our files also hold the 1949 Superboy.
author: Karl Kesel, Ron Marz

subject: series
synopsis: DC's team-up showcase (1955-1983): tryouts for the Justice League and Teen Titans, then Bob Haney and Jim Aparo's long run of Batman team-ups.
author: Bob Haney, Gerry Conway

subject: series
synopsis: Thing team-up series from the 70s-80s. A warm-hearted Bronze Age institution — Ben Grimm's gruff charm works surprisingly well with almost any partner. Consistently entertaining.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The US print/digital edition of Viz Media's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, providing English-language access to chapters of One Piece, Naruto, Bleach, and other flagship Jump titles simultaneously with their Japanese releases — a landmark in legal simultaneous manga distribution.

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas and Jean-Marc Lofficier's 90s Strange series. A loving if overwrought extension of the character's mythology, best enjoyed by dedicated fans of Marvel's supernatural corner.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 'non-team' of anti-social heroes. The Englehart/Sal Buscema era is solid Bronze Age Marvel; Matt Fraction's witty five-issue mini is a modern delight; the Bendis street-level Netflix-adjacent run is also well-regarded.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Wolverine's 2003 series: Greg Rucka's grounded opening, Mark Millar and John Romita Jr.'s Enemy of the State, then Guggenheim and Jason Aaron.
author: Mark Millar, Marc Guggenheim

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's anthology hosted by the horror legend's image. Gentle mystery and horror stories typical of the Gold Key anthology style — not scary, but charmingly macabre.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's short-lived Mad Magazine competitor. Some sharp satire but rarely matching its inspiration's consistency.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hulk volume 2 (2000-2008): Paul Jenkins's opening, Bruce Jones's long paranoid-thriller run, Peter David's brief return and Greg Pak's Planet Hulk.

subject: series
synopsis: Zenescope's fairy tale horror anthology with extensive 'cheesecake' covers. Occasionally interesting takes on dark fairy tale source material; more often exploitative packaging undermines the content.

subject: series
synopsis: Yukinobu Tatsu's breakout manga combines alien abductions, traditional Japanese spirits, and teenage romance in a gloriously chaotic package. The kinetic art and genuine warmth of character make it one of the most exciting contemporary manga.
author: Yukinobu Tatsu

subject: series
synopsis: Harvey Comics' run on the classic Otto Messmer character. Cheerful absurdist humor with Felix and his magic bag of tricks. Historical significance is primarily about the character's iconic status in animation.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's acclaimed Marvel run on Darth Vader, picking up immediately after The Empire Strikes Back and charting Vader's obsessive hunt for the truth about Luke Skywalker while navigating Imperial politics, illustrated with cinematic scope.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's 2011 series: Wolverine reopens Xavier's school as the Jean Grey School, with Chris Bachalo and Nick Bradshaw's art and Quentin Quire's mischief.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's quarterly 1993-2003 oversized X-Men anthology of standalone character stories by rotating creative teams.
author: Chuck Austen, Steven Grant

subject: series
synopsis: Kouji Seo's music romance manga. Emotionally ambitious but divisive — a shocking mid-series plot development is either brave or gratuitous depending on tolerance for melodrama.
author: Kouji Seo

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Conway's 1982 Firestorm ongoing — Ronnie Raymond and Martin Stein fused as the Nuclear Man — later John Ostrander's darker Firestorm, the Nuclear Man era.
author: Gerry Conway, John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Atlas/Marvel's 1952 fantasy-horror anthology that introduced Thor in #83 (1962), with Lee, Kirby and Ditko monster tales before it.
author: Larry Lieber, Robert Bernstein

subject: series
synopsis: The legendary London edition of OZ, the psychedelic underground magazine edited by Richard Neville, Jim Anderson and Felix Dennis from 1967 to 1973, fusing radical politics, sexual liberation, drugs and rock music with Martin Sharp's hallucinatory graphic design. Its 1971 'Schoolkids' issue (OZ 28) sparked the longest obscenity trial in British history, making it a defining artefact of the counterculture and the underground press.
author: Richard Neville

subject: series
synopsis: Jean-Paul Valley's post-Knightfall series. Dennis O'Neil keeps the character's religious extremism and moral instability as ongoing threads — a character study of someone ill-suited to heroism.
author: Dennis O'Neil

subject: series
synopsis: Alex de Campi's digital series for Thrillbent: a soldier in Napoleon's retreat from Moscow is drawn into a war between supernatural beings.

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Perry's long-running Antarctic Press manga-style adventure: genius archaeologist Gina Diggers and her werecheetah sister Brittany raid tombs and dimensions.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1989-1996 Star Trek: The Next Generation ongoing: original adventures of Picard's crew, written largely by Michael Jan Friedman.

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan North and Iban Coello's 2022 Fantastic Four: the scattered family solving strange, clever done-in-one science puzzles across America.
author: Ryan North

subject: series
synopsis: Justice League International renamed (1989-1996): Giffen and DeMatteis's bwa-ha-ha comedy era, then Dan Jurgens and Gerard Jones.
author: Dan Vado, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: DC's second Star Trek ongoing (1989-1996): Kirk's crew after Star Trek V, opened by Peter David and carried for years by Howard Weinstein.

subject: series
synopsis: Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark manga is one of the greatest achievements in comics. The sprawling psychic-powers dystopia set in Neo-Tokyo influenced science fiction and visual storytelling globally. Dense, ambiguous, and visually extraordinary.
author: Katsuhiro Otomo

subject: series
synopsis: Johns and Lee's New 52 launch combined blockbuster action with soap opera plotting. Snyder's later run aimed for Hickman-scale ambition. An accessible entry point to DC's premier team.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Kentaro Miura's dark fantasy manga is one of the greatest long-form comics works ever created. Guts's quest through a nightmarish medieval world is harrowing, philosophical, and visually extraordinary. Its influence on visual media is immeasurable.
author: Kentaro Miura

subject: series
synopsis: Benjamin Percy's Krakoa-era X-Force positions the team as mutantkind's CIA, with Wolverine, Beast, and Jean Grey navigating espionage and moral compromise in defense of the nation-state of Krakoa.
author: Benjamin Percy

subject: series
synopsis: Peter David's 1994 Aquaman: Arthur loses a hand and grows harsher in the hook-handed run, later Erik Larsen and Dan Jurgens.
author: Peter Allen David - 'PAD', Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: Deadpool's 2008 series by Daniel Way and Paco Medina, from Secret Invasion through the inner-voices era to #63 and the #900 specials.
author: Daniel Way

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas's legacy series following children of the Justice Society. DC's first serious multi-generational superhero saga; valuable for Golden Age character continuity.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Mantlo and Sal Buscema's Hasbro-licensed Spaceknight (1979-1986): Rom hunts the shape-shifting Dire Wraiths on Earth inside the Marvel Universe.
author: Bill Mantlo

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Darick Robertson's gleefully transgressive satire about a CIA black-ops team that polices a world of corrupt, celebrity-worshipping superheroes. A vicious, profane, and occasionally genuinely moving deconstruction of superhero power fantasy and corporate America, it became the basis for Amazon's hit TV series.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Joss Whedon and John Cassaday's celebrated 2004-2008 run, opening with 'Gifted' and the discovery of a mutant 'cure.' Razor-sharp dialogue, blockbuster Cassaday artwork, the resurrection of Colossus, and the Breakworld saga made it a modern X-Men high point.
author: Joss Whedon

subject: series
synopsis: Morris and René Goscinny's beloved Belgian Western comedy series featuring the fastest draw in the West; a charming, witty parody of Western tropes with Goscinny's sharp humour at its peak, a cornerstone of Franco-Belgian comics.
author: René Goscinny

subject: series
synopsis: The original Superboy (1949-1977): Clark Kent's boyhood adventures in Smallville, sharing the title with the Legion of Super-Heroes from #197.
author: Paul Levitz, Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Fabian Nicieza and Mark Bagley's team book launched a fresh-faced squad — Night Thrasher, Nova, Firestar, Speedball, Namorita, Marvel Boy — fighting villains outside the Avengers' shadow. Strong characterization and ensemble dynamics made it a standout of early-1990s Marvel.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Thunderbolts from #100 (2006-2012): Warren Ellis and Mike Deodato's Norman Osborn era, Andy Diggle, then Jeff Parker's Luke Cage-led prison team.

subject: series
synopsis: Jay Faerber's superhero soap opera follows the Noble family — a famous superhero dynasty — through the scandals, secrets, and betrayals that come with being the world's most public powered family.
author: Jay Faerber

subject: series
synopsis: G. Willow Wilson's limited series elevated Pamela Isley beyond villain into complex eco-terrorist anti-hero. The recent ongoing explores environmental themes with genuine emotional investment.
author: G. Willow Wilson

subject: series
synopsis: Abnett and Lanning's 2008 Annihilation-adjacent revival gave the team cosmic purpose and sharp character dynamics. The Bendis era that followed was more mainstream-accessible. Essential for Marvel cosmic fans.
author: Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's continuation of Larry Hama's Marvel G.I. Joe from #155 (2010-2022), picking up the original numbering where Marvel stopped in 1994.
author: Larry Hama

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's late 90s Justice League run restored the team to A-list status after years of decline. Rock star heroes, mythological scale threats, and inventive storytelling. Essential superhero comics.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Johnny Blaze's first ongoing (1973-1983): the stunt rider bonded to the demon Zarathos, by Gary Friedrich, Michael Fleisher and Roger Stern.
author: Roger McKenzie, Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor's prequel comics to the video game are dramatically better than their origin warrants. A What If Superman snapped? scenario executed with genuine emotional weight.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: The Licensed Extra-Governmental Interstellar Operatives Network polices the galaxy.
author: Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: The companion series to Legion of Super-Heroes in the 90s, set in a pocket-universe Batch SW6. Complex continuity work by Tom McCraw and Mark Waid.
author: Tom McCraw

subject: series
synopsis: Abnett and Lanning's 2007 Nova: Richard Rider as the last Nova Centurion, carrying the Worldmind out of Annihilation into War of Kings.
author: Andy Lanning

subject: series
synopsis: The British adult humor comic — crude, anarchic, and enduringly popular. Roger Mellie, Johnny Fartpants, and the Fat Slags are cultural institutions of a very particular British comedy tradition.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's mutant pop singer. The early issues have charming 80s naivety as a disco-era character whose moment had already passed; Tom DeFalco's later run improves as the character finds purpose.
author: Tom DeFalco

subject: series
synopsis: Doctor Strange's 1974 series: Englehart and Brunner's cosmic opening, Gene Colan's long run, and Roger Stern with Marshall Rogers and Paul Smith.
author: Roger Stern, J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Tom King and Daniel Sampere's 2023 Wonder Woman: Diana outlawed by the U.S. government and hunted by the Sovereign, framed by tales of her daughter Trinity.

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's cat-and-mouse comedy comics. The animated energy doesn't always translate but the all-ages humor is consistent.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Digital-first comics based on the Teen Titans Go! cartoon: gag stories with Robin, Starfire, Raven, Beast Boy and Cyborg.

subject: series
synopsis: The Legion's 1984 Baxter-paper series: Paul Levitz's long run with Keith Giffen, Steve Lightle and Greg LaRocque.
author: Paul Levitz, Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Dan Mora's recent DC series is one of the finest Superman/Batman team-up works — warm, optimistic, and visually spectacular. Mora's dynamic layouts are extraordinary.
author: Mark Waid

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Azzarello and Cliff Chiang's New 52 Wonder Woman (2011-2014): Diana as daughter of Zeus amid a savage Olympian family feud, then the Finches.
author: Christopher Priest

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's flagship X-Men series of the Krakoa era, following a team assembled by a public vote who serve as Earth's mutant champions while navigating the complex politics of the island nation.
author: Gerry Duggan

subject: series
synopsis: Oliver Queen's 1988 series: Mike Grell's grounded urban-hunter run after The Longbow Hunters, then Chuck Dixon, ending with Connor Hawke's succession.
author: Charles 'Chuck' Dixon, Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Epic Collection reprints of Master of Kung Fu, the acclaimed Bronze Age series featuring Shang-Chi, Son of Fu Manchu, in globe-spanning martial arts espionage adventures drawn with kinetic energy by Paul Gulacy.
author: Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Where the Justice Society of America was born — the first ever team of superheroes in a single comic book. Historically irreplaceable. The Roy Thomas revival in the 70s is also very good.
author: Gardner Fox

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's weekly anthology that mixed US reprints with original British material. Captain Britain, Night-Raven, and other UK-created characters appeared here alongside the American content.
